source_quote: The Arab Renaissance is studied through historical and socio-political texts.
answer: CVLN 181 Arab Renaissance, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the Arab Renaissance studied through historical and socio-political texts.

source_quote: This course provides an overview of art and its development in the Western world. It
answer: CVLN 190 Freshman Art History, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: overview of Western art from Prehistoric to Contemporary Art and the influence of socio-political cultures.

source_quote: This course covers reading and interpreting electrical installation drawings and
answer: ELEC 101 Electrical Drawing, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: reading and producing electrical installation, machine and circuit drawings with standard symbols and computer packages, and building wiring systems.

source_quote: The course will introduce and cover circuit variables and elements; methods and
answer: ELEC 111 Industrial Electricity, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: circuit variables and elements, DC and AC circuit analysis, 3-phase systems, power calculations, and industrial devices and safety.

source_quote: This course introduces different logic gates, develops truth tables for combinational
answer: ELEC 121 Digital Electronics, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: logic gates, truth tables for combinational circuits, simple Boolean expressions, and basic IC concepts.

source_quote: This course aims to provide a basic understanding of the principles of analog
answer: ELEC 122 Analog Electronics, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: principles of analog electronics, diodes, transistors, op amps, and basic amplifier design.

source_quote: This course provides a basic knowledge of circuitry for the control and conversion of
answer: ELEC 123 Industrial Electronics, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: power control and conversion circuitry such as DC-DC converters, AC-DC rectifiers, and DC-AC inverters.

source_quote: This course covers the principles of electrical power generation and distribution, as
answer: ELEC 131 Electrical Power Generation and Distribution, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: principles of power generation and distribution and power system protection.

source_quote: This course covers the construction, principles of operation, characteristics, and
answer: ELEC 132 Electric Machines, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: DC machines, transformer basics, and AC machines (construction, operation, applications).

source_quote: This course teaches students the basics of drawing with lines, shapes, tones, shadows,
answer: FADR 100 Basic Drawing, 3(2,2), a freshman elective: drawing with lines, shapes, tones, shadows and color using still life and media such as charcoal, pencil, graphite and ink.

source_quote: This course is a comprehensive overview of artistic movements throughout the
answer: FADR 115 History of Art Overview, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: artistic movements across centuries with emphasis on the 20th century, and tools for analyzing art in context.

source_quote: This course focuses on the principles, theories, and applications of additive and
answer: FADR 120 Introduction to Color Theory, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: additive and subtractive color, color schemes, mixing, properties and relationships, and the psychological and cultural meaning of color.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the basic concepts and practices of digital
answer: FADR 130 Basic Digital Photography, 3(2,2), a freshman elective: using cameras and lenses, composition, exposure, light and color, digital manipulation, formats and resolution.

source_quote: This course introduces students to Arabic Calligraphy, one of the highest art forms in
answer: GRDS 150 Introduction to Arabic Calligraphy, 3(2,2), a freshman elective: history, tools and styles of Islamic calligraphy (Riqa, Naskh, Deewani, Thuluth, Kufi) with hands-on lettering and Kufic compositions.

source_quote: This course introduces the basic principles of advertising and their role in media and
answer: GRDS 160 Principles of Advertising, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: advertising principles, the industry and agencies, client relationships, audiences, media, ethics, creative strategy, and advertising history.

source_quote: This course examines various topics, including the origins of civilization in Egypt and
answer: HIST 100 History of the Ancient World, 3(3,0): origins of civilization in Egypt and Mesopotamia, Ancient Greece and Rome, Judaism, and the early Christian Church. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: A survey of European history begins with the 16th-century Protestant Reformation and
answer: HIST 102 Europe from the Reformation to the French Revolution, 3(3,0): the Protestant Reformation, absolutism, the scientific revolution, the Enlightenment, the Old Regime, and the French Revolution. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: Topics include the Industrial Revolution; the rise of political ideologies, social classes,
answer: HIST 103 Europe in the 19th and 20th Centuries, 3(3,0): the Industrial Revolution, ideologies, nationalism, imperialism, the Russian Revolution, both world wars, and the Cold War. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: American history from 1607 to 1877 examines the development of the United States
answer: HIST 108 Issues and Themes in U.S. History: 1607-1877, 3(3,0): U.S. development from early settlement through the Civil War, politics, race relations, economic and social trends, and westward expansion. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: This introductory course is designed to provide a general overview of some aspects of
answer: GEOL 160 Earth Geology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: Earth's natural environment, physical systems and processes, and their environmental effects.

source_quote: This course is an introduction to the part of philosophy concerned with questions about
answer: PHIL 102 Freshman Philosophy, 3(3,0): questions about the nature of the world and knowledge, God, reality, human nature, skepticism, freedom and determinism, and mind and body. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: This course introduces the basic rules of clear and rational thought. Students are
answer: PHIL 110 Critical Thinking, 3(3,0): rules of clear rational thought, detecting false reasoning, emotional appeals and contradictions, and building clear arguments.

source_quote: English speakers or English 098. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.
answer: PHIL 110 Critical Thinking requires being a native English speaker or English 098 as prerequisite and ENGL 101 as co-requisite.

source_quote: This survey course is recommended for students interested in discovering how politics
answer: POSC 190 Freshman Politics, 3(3,0): how politics affects lives; basics of political theory, comparative politics, international relations, and public policy. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: This course aims to develop an understanding of human psychology by focusing on
answer: PSYC 190 Freshman Psychology, 3(3,0): cognition, emotions, learning, development, biological bases of behavior, personality, disorders, psychotherapy, and social behavior. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: This course addresses the basic principles, theories, and techniques to manage
answer: PSYC 195 Freshman Stress Management, 3(3,0): principles and techniques for managing personal stress, the mind-body relationship, and coping and relaxation techniques. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: This course is designed to give freshman students an overview of the field and
answer: SOCI 190 Freshman Sociology, 3(3,0): essential sociological concepts, the individual in society, social institutions, and how social forces and human action shape lived experience. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: Students are expected to finish the Freshman Program in two regular semesters.
answer: Freshman students are expected to finish the program in two regular semesters and can register for up to 15 credits per semester; freshman students on probation can register for at most 12 credits.

source_quote: Students must take BECN 190 and achieve a minimum grade of 70.
answer: To transfer from Freshman Science to Freshman Arts, a student must take BECN 190 and achieve a minimum grade of 70.

source_quote: IELP 100 13
answer: A freshman's English level on acceptance sets their credit limit alongside the English course: IELP 085 - 10 credits, IELP 095 - 10 credits, IELP 100 - 13 credits.

source_quote: If the students’ English level upon acceptance is ENGL 210, ENGL 210 replaces ENGL
answer: If a freshman student places at ENGL 210, ENGL 210 replaces ENGL 101, and ENGL 210 is then replaced by a humanities elective in the degree program.

source_quote: To take humanities or social sciences courses, students should consider the following:
answer: Humanities/social sciences courses numbered 100-level have ENGL 101 as co-requisite, 200-level have ENGL 101 as prerequisite, and 300-level are tied to ENGL 210.

source_quote: Students may join a degree-granting program at RHU after completing the freshman
answer: After the freshman program, students may join a degree program if they obtain the freshman-to-Lebanese Baccalaureate equivalency from the MoEHE Equivalence Committee. Freshman Arts students may join any Business program, Graphic Design, or English; Freshman Science students may join any degree program at RHU.

source_quote: Graphic Design Program. A GPA of at least 70 and a passing score on the RHU
answer: Freshman students joining Graphic Design need a GPA of at least 70 and a passing score on the RHU Graphic Design Aptitude Test.

source_quote: Computer Science Program: A GPA of at least 70 and a minimum grade of 70 in MATH
answer: Freshman students joining Computer Science or Healthcare Information Systems need a GPA of at least 70 and a minimum grade of 70 in MATH 190 and MATH 191.

source_quote: Business Administration programs. A GPA of at least 70 and a grade of at least 70 in
answer: Freshman students joining Business Administration programs need a GPA of at least 70 and a grade of at least 70 in MATH 189 or MATH 190 and in BECN 190.

source_quote: Engineering Programs. A GPA of at least 70 and a minimum grade of 70 in MATH 190,
answer: Freshman students joining Engineering programs need a GPA of at least 70 and a minimum grade of 70 in MATH 190, MATH 191, PHYS 190, and PHYS 191.
